open_decisions.title: Engine, platform and deployment candidates
open_decisions.description: Select tested Godot/export-template and Unicode-data revisions, supported client platforms, trusted identity provider, persistence implementation and initial hosting. The documented headless/small modular relational approach is a defensible starting recommendation; vendors and capacity are unspecified.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-001/BW-018 choose and demonstrate tested candidates; BW-086/BW-088 verify external-play deployment and compatibility.

open_decisions.title: Capacity, security and recovery budgets
open_decisions.description: Approve concrete per-endpoint lifetimes/limits/retention, expected workload, tick/tail-latency/bandwidth budgets, recovery point/time and release admission envelope. Prototype rates and 20-second grace are starting settings, not established achievements.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before the relevant security/restore/load epic is Complete; final release cannot accept unnamed or unmeasured targets.

open_decisions.title: Concrete world and starter records
open_decisions.description: Author finite functional maps, appearance assets, starter instructions, NPC kits, loot tables, recovery/exit locations and required XP allocations within existing contracts. No names, lore, branching narrative system or detailed new geography are inferred here.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative records before BW-039; full-roster starter and level 11–60 content before BW-052/BW-053, and reviewed release-content manifest before BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Runtime bindings and complete release inventory
open_decisions.description: Prototype profiles do not establish the named secondary ability/talent behavior. The supplied 257 recipes and sample items are representative, not the launch inventory. Decide concrete compatible bindings and complete useful content within the documented class/profession scope.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-047–051 and BW-062 certify the intended full scope; BW-092 rejects missing required roster/content rather than silently shrinking the game.

open_decisions.title: Prices, sources and conversion graph
open_decisions.description: Concrete vendor values, recipe conversion values, source distributions, starter XP allocation and economic tuning need authoring and tests. Published fees, six bands and profession relevance targets remain prototype constraints, not measured health.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before enabling the relevant vendor/conversion content; economy/profession measurement in BW-072 and final integration in BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Measured balance, usability and content limits
open_decisions.description: Approve balance deviations and launch content bounds using equal-budget role/build/faction tests, actual progression, supported input devices and accessible visual feedback. Twelve classes, 37 specializations and level cap 60 remain requirements; a smaller technical slice is not permission to omit them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative proof before expansion; BW-071–074 and BW-092 resolve release-blocking findings using documented test standards.

open_decisions.title: Incremental topology and comparable branch orders
open_decisions.description: A small deployment with explicit loading transitions can validate the required game before fleet complexity. Full-state conservative recovery is sufficient under the documented baseline; no exact lost-tick replay, unrestricted rewind or seamless travel requirement is added. Social/profession branches can move earlier if team capacity supports them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Revisit after BW-083/BW-082 measurements and before BW-090 capacity approval; change ordering while retaining IDs if evidence contradicts the assumption.

open_decisions.title: Concrete item-use timing bindings
open_decisions.description: Authored consumable effect records specify effects, channels and category/recipient restrictions. Any unspecified consumption, interruption/refund and treatment-lock start timing needs an explicit reviewed runtime binding before that item is enabled; do not infer it from animation or let duplicate use choose a favorable policy.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before BW-075 is Complete; preserve published durations, caps, mode exclusions and authoritative conservation.

open_decisions.title: Rated entry eligibility and normalized build selection
open_decisions.description: Rated combat requires effective level 60 and a 118-point budget, but the reference does not specify minimum actual entry level or how a below-cap entrant selects legal normalized talents, role services and ability unlocks. Decide whether entry requires actual level 60 or supports lower-level entrants with an explicitly reviewed temporary build/ability policy. Preserve the required normalization and ordinary earned progression; this audit selects neither alternative.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Approve before BW-067 can be Complete and before BW-068 admits rated participants. Test admitted-level entry/exit/reconnect, temporary mode selections and unchanged ordinary build/progression; do not infer match initialization or respawn policy from ordinary build application.

open_decisions.title: Render configuration and supported quality envelope
open_decisions.description: The 3D pixel-art direction is selected. Pin the tested renderer/backend/platform envelope, orthographic pitch/framing, internal resolution, pixel scale and aspect/minimum-window policy, asset/material/animation conventions, shadow/outline/pass strategy, environmental quality tiers and client frame/memory budgets. Do not invent fixed resolutions, require an engine fork or promise unsupported renderer parity from the article.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-097 resolves feasibility, camera/display defaults and any engine patch decision; BW-098 fixes production conventions; BW-099 demonstrates environment methods and alternatives; BW-074/BW-090 approve the supported release visual and performance matrix.

deferred_scope: Neutral/cross-faction exchanges, war logistics, timed auctions and financial instruments are outside the baseline economy; neither faction depends on enemy supply. Faction-local fixed-price listings and buyer requests remain required.
Race/faction transfers and class changes are not launch capabilities. Optional cosmetic account collections grant no account-wide combat power or profession throughput.

Housing, territory, sieges, authored geography/lore and long offline manufacturing are outside the current documented baseline. This roadmap requires functional maps/assets/content, without inventing worldbuilding.

Voice chat and seamless travel are optional, not prerequisites. Explicit transitions and a small deployment satisfy the initial topology; larger raid sizes and fleet growth require authored limits and measurements.
No required catalog family is silently deferred beyond the full-game gate. Incomplete bespoke content remains disabled during earlier slices and must be bound/certified for the intended full roster.
critical_review: Moved the durable ownership/recovery probe into the first review group so database correctness can be tested alongside simulation instead of waiting for a full role encounter. It has no combat dependency.

Kept privacy in the initial entity projection and added richer relevance bounds before the first integrated action. Prediction follows authoritative movement but is a recommendation for the technical proof, not a fabricated prerequisite of numerical combat.

Introduced a representative signature-resource probe before role and starter integration; full pets, forms, maintained support and damage-debt families precede roster expansion, rather than every first playable interaction.

Separated a representative beginner playtest from full-roster level 1–10 certification. Optional crafting and grouping remain optional to a player, while the documented introductions still need integration evidence.

Separated local travel and instance identity from cross-process ownership. Simple handoff is tested before final advanced-state recovery; the first handoff does not certify mechanics introduced afterward.

Removed global phase barriers and kept social, profession and economic branches independently actionable. Recommended predecessors express integration convenience; only observable prerequisites are hard edges.

Required provider security and a real restore before persistent external testing, while early headless fixtures and restricted technical sessions stay small. Final capacity and incidents wait for representative full workloads.

Retained separate full-game integration and release gates. Completion percentages describe epic counts only; undefined capacity, balance targets or launch-content bounds cannot be replaced by optimistic status updates.

A competent team could move some profession/social work earlier or defer a simple handoff until larger zones exist. This order favors earlier conservation/ownership learning; it makes no claim that those comparable branch orders have a unique optimum.

Independent audit: retain the initial network/replication order, add explicit content production and a combined-family probe, enforce only demonstrated hard prerequisites, and leave rated entry/build selection as an explicit unresolved policy. See the Roadmap Audit for baseline evidence and per-epic dispositions.

Art-direction revision: replaced the former 2D sprite mandate with the user-selected 3D pixel-art reference. Added BW-097/BW-098/BW-099 for early renderer feasibility, reusable art production and environment integration, retaining independent headless work and requiring complete visual/performance evidence at existing release gates.
maintenance: Edit only sources/development-roadmap.json for planning content, statuses, blockers and evidence. Do not hand-edit the generated pages, dashboard, milestone states, search records or manifest counts. Status must be exactly Not Started, In Progress, Blocked or Complete.

For an existing epic, change status and add verified_evidence records with criteria (one-based AC numbers), artifact (a committed repository-relative file or HTTPS evidence link), revision (the tested game/content revision), result (Passed or Failed) and summary. Preserve prior failure evidence in retained run artifacts; the current completion record must have passing evidence for every criterion. Never copy documentation-validation results into gameplay-completion evidence.

A Blocked epic needs a concrete blockers entry identifying the unresolved decision, missing prerequisite or external limit. Ordinary future prerequisites do not make every unstarted epic Blocked. Reopen an epic when a regression invalidates its current evidence; update dependent completion states rather than leaving a false release gate.

To insert work, allocate a new unused BW ID without renumbering existing epics. Put it at a dependency-valid position, choose its phase, add feature coverage and include it in applicable milestone/integration requirements. Gaps are allowed; IDs must never be reused for a different capability. Do not alter canonical gameplay contracts merely to classify planning documentation.

Each epic is published at guide/roadmap-bw-NNN.html with a stable BW identifier and BW-NNN-AC-N criterion links. Use the epic as the parent for future tickets and link each ticket to its covered criteria and verification evidence. Keep criterion numbering aligned with recorded evidence; introduce actual ticket records only when ticket planning is performed.

Run the commands below after a status or evidence edit. The first rebuilds all derived progress, readiness and HTML pages from the registry. The inventory review refreshes the generated planning-page fingerprints, navigation, search and page counts. The focused validator checks graph, coverage, evidence and output consistency; the existing full check also includes roadmap validation.

Store implementation tickets in this same registry with stable BW-NNN-TNN IDs, parent_epic and exact epic_criteria anchors. Keep tickets in dependency order and cover every criterion of each split epic. Each ticket defines scope, exclusions, observable acceptance criteria, completion evidence and a runnable manual test with launch, setup, actions, expected results and reset, or an explicit non-applicability rationale. Include required test fixtures and controls in implementation scope. Track ticket status, blockers and verified evidence separately; planning or ticket progress never automatically completes an epic. Complete tickets require actual passing evidence for every ticket criterion and completed dependencies.

tickets.title: Pin the Godot 4.7 toolchain and macOS baseline
scope: Inspect the existing project.godot baseline: Godot 4.7, Forward Plus, Jolt and a Windows D3D12 preference are declared, but there are no scenes, scripts, export presets or build tools. Preserve Godot 4.7 as requested; identify its exact release or development build and source revision rather than substituting another minor version.

Create tools/toolchain.lock.json with the exact engine and matching export-template versions, acquisition locations and checksums, macOS version/CPU architecture used for verification, required Python version, and any source build instructions. Record no engine patches for the initial stock build, or explicitly pin an existing patch set without adopting a new fork.

Record macOS client and macOS dedicated headless server as the verified BW-001 targets. Linux and Windows are future targets, with no compatibility claim until tested. Record the provisional client Forward Plus/backend settings separately from headless simulation, retaining the Windows setting only as an unverified future-platform preference.

Add tools/verify_toolchain.py and setup instructions that verify the lock against locally acquired engine/templates, report exact paths and mismatches, and work without a preexisting project import cache. Provide a temporary lock-copy option for negative checks.
out_of_scope: Selecting a different Godot minor version; renderer feasibility, camera, shaders, art assets or new engine patches (BW-097).
Linux/Windows execution, release signing/notarization, hosting, gameplay or automated downloads using credentials.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh macOS environment can acquire the exact recorded Godot 4.7 build and matching templates by following the setup instructions; checksum/version verification succeeds and records the native CPU target.
A missing engine, missing templates or modified checksum in a temporary lock copy returns a nonzero exit and identifies the missing/mismatched component with a corrective action.
The lock separates provisional client renderer/backend settings from the headless target and explicitly records the engine patch state; it identifies Linux and Windows as future unverified targets.
